It achieves this by removing Part 3 of the Qantas Sale Act 1992 and changing the Air Navigation Act 1920 so Qantas is treated like other Australian international airlines. Foreign ownership of Qantas is currently capped at 49 per cent total, 25 per cent for a single investor and 35 per cent for foreign airlines, but the bill would repeal all these limits.. Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) Amendment (Classification Tools and Other Measures) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Attorney-General. This bill would update Australia's national classification system for publications, films and computer games based on initial recommendations from a law reform review. It would allow automated classification tools, require classification markings on all rated content, and let the Attorney-General's Department alert police about potentially refused-classification material without a prior decision. The bill also makes minor amendments, including giving the minister explicit power to set rules for displaying consumer advice and replacing the requirement for Senior Classifiers with a discretion to appoint them.. Consumers, film and computer game distributors, festivals, cultural institutions, the Classification Board, the Attorney-General's Department, and law enforcement authorities.

title: Intellectual Property Laws Amendment Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Industry. The bill would make changes to several intellectual property laws to improve the system. It would allow Australian drug makers to seek a court order to produce generic versions of patented medicines for export to eligible developing countries. The patent holder would be paid compensation negotiated to avoid disadvantaging them.. Australian pharmaceutical manufacturers, patent holders, and developing countries that meet specified criteria.

Defence Force Retirement Benefits Legislation Amendment (Fair Indexation) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Veterans’ Affairs. The bill would change how certain military retirement pensions are increased each year for pensioners aged 55 or older. From 1 July 2014, those pensions would be indexed using the same method as age and service pensions, comparing consumer price index, living cost index and male total average weekly earnings. The new indexation would apply to DFRB and DFRDB retirement, invalidity and reversionary pensions, but not to child and orphan pensions.. Defence Force Retirement Benefits and Defence Force Retirement and Death Benefits pensioners aged 55 or older, including surviving spouses and associates from family law splits.

title: Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals Legislation Amendment (Removing Re-approval and Re-registration) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Agriculture. The bill would remove the need to re-approve and re-register agricultural and veterinary chemicals under the Agvet Code. It would delete end dates for approvals and allow registrations to be renewed without a final renewal, while also cutting red tape and improving regulator access to safety information. The bill also amends the Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals Legislation Amendment Act 2013, the Food Standards Australia New Zealand Act 1991, and the Collection Act, with no start date specified in the outline.. Manufacturers, importers, and users of agricultural and veterinary chemicals, as well as the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority (APVMA).

title: Omnibus Repeal Day (Autumn 2014) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Prime Minister. The bill would remove or change laws across ten government portfolios to cut red tape for businesses, individuals and community groups. It would simplify what telecom providers must report, drop duplicate building certification for aged care, and let small-scale importers skip ozone-protection licensing. The bill also deletes several Acts that are no longer needed, including one that created two construction-industry bodies, one of which was shut down in 1995 and the other has no current members.. Businesses, individuals and the community sector affected by regulation in ten portfolios, plus telecommunications providers, aged care providers, low-volume importers, and entities linked to the repealed construction-industry and housing Acts.

title: Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment Bill 2014
snippet: lapsed. Employment. This bill would cut red tape for businesses covered by the Comcare workers' compensation scheme. It would let the regulator grant a single self-insurance licence to a group of related companies instead of requiring each to apply separately. The government says the changes would save the economy $32.8 million each year for the next 10 years.. Australian Government and ACT employees, employees of licensed private corporations, and corporations seeking self-insurance under the Comcare scheme.

title: Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (Repeal) (No. 1) Bill 2014
snippet: lapsed. Social Services. This bill would abolish the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission. It would repeal the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission Act 2012, but would not take effect until a later bill is enacted to set up replacement arrangements. The bill would also provide transitional rules for transferring records, handling outstanding Ombudsman investigations, and continuing protection for information disclosed under the Act.. Charities and not-for-profit organisations that are registered with the Commission.

title: Australian National Preventive Health Agency (Abolition) Bill 2014
snippet: lapsed. Health. The bill would close the Australian National Preventive Health Agency. Preventive health tasks shared between two federal bodies would be merged into the Department of Health to cut duplication and costs. The bill would end the roles of the agency's chief executive, staff, advisory council and committees, and transfer leftover work to the Department of Health.. The Australian National Preventive Health Agency, its staff and advisory bodies, and the Commonwealth Department of Health.

title: Health Workforce Australia (Abolition) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Health. This bill would abolish the independent body Health Workforce Australia (HWA). HWA's functions and programmes would move to the Commonwealth Department of Health, and its assets, liabilities, contracts and other instruments would be transferred. The government says the change would reduce duplication and bureaucracy and improve the delivery of health workforce policy.. Health Workforce Australia and the Commonwealth Department of Health.

title: G20 (Safety and Security) Complementary Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Justice. The bill would create a new Commonwealth Act to clarify how Queensland's G20 safety law interacts with federal law at Brisbane Airport during the 2014 G20 Summit. It would provide mechanisms for resolving overlaps between the Queensland G20 Act and existing Commonwealth legislation at the airport, which is a Commonwealth place. The bill would ensure police and authorised persons clearly understand which powers they can use at Brisbane Airport during the summit.. Police officers and other appointed or authorised persons at Brisbane Airport during the G20 Summit.

title: Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Attorney-General. The bill would make Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants pay an annual registration charge to recover the cost of regulating them. Celebrants who do not pay the charge, unless exempted, would be deregistered, and regulations would set out exemption processes and grounds. The charge would apply from 1 July 2013, and the amendments in Schedule 1, Part 4 would apply from 1 July 2014 or later.. Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants, including those from independent religious organisations, and aspiring marriage celebrants.

title: Marriage (Celebrant Registration Charge) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Attorney-General. This bill would introduce an annual cost recovery levy for Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants. The charge would apply to celebrants registered on or after 1 July in a financial year, with exemptions available through regulations. The measure was originally part of a 2011-12 Budget announcement intended to start from 1 July 2013 but was delayed due to the previous bill not passing before Parliament was prorogued.. Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants, including those from independent religious organisations whose denominations are not proclaimed under section 26 of the Marriage Act.

snippet: passed. Treasury. The bill would lower compliance costs for financial advisers by changing key parts of the Future of Financial Advice laws. It would remove the requirement for clients to renew ongoing fee arrangements every two years and make fee disclosure statements only apply to agreements starting after 1 July 2013. The explanatory memorandum says the government consulted with consumer and industry groups and made refinements based on that feedback.. Financial advisers and their clients.

snippet: passed. Attorney-General. The bill would create a standard set of regulatory powers that Commonwealth agencies can use across different laws. Agencies would gain monitoring and investigation powers, plus enforcement tools such as civil penalties, infringement notices, enforceable undertakings and injunctions. The powers would be rolled out progressively, with new or amended laws needing to trigger the bill's provisions through primary legislation.. Commonwealth regulatory agencies and the regulatory schemes they administer.

title: Student Identifiers Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Industry. The bill would create a unique student identifier for people doing nationally recognised vocational education and training from 1 January 2015. A Student Identifiers Registrar would assign, collect, use and disclose the identifier and maintain an authenticated transcript of each student's record. The bill sets up a confidentiality scheme that prohibits collecting, using or disclosing identifiers without authorisation, except in prescribed circumstances, and requires destruction of personal information collected solely for the identifier application.. Individuals undertaking nationally recognised vocational education and training, registered training organisations, and state, territory and Commonwealth governments.

The bill would also amend the Australian Meat and Live-stock Industry Act 1997 to let the department recover costs for quota arrangements run by other countries.. snippet: passed. Agriculture. snippet: passed. Agriculture. title: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Mental Health and Other Measures) Bill 2014
snippet: passed. Veterans’ Affairs. The bill would change the Veterans' Entitlements Act from 1 July 2014 to broaden who can get free mental health care and which conditions qualify. It would extend non-liability health care to cover alcohol and substance use disorders, and to include former Australian Defence Force members who served for at least three years and were discharged because they could not perform their duties. The expansion applies to those with three or more years of continuous full-time peacetime service starting on or after 7 April 1994, including those with service both before and after that date.. Veterans and former Australian Defence Force members with qualifying service.
